newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian Norilsk Nickel 96 output detailed by Tass.
newsitem.headline: Russian Norilsk Nickel 96 output detailed by Tass.

text.p: Russia's RAO Norilsk Nickel metals group saw its 1996 nickel output slip to 177,185 tonnes, Itar-Tass news agency's joint-venture Prime-Tass said on Tuesday.
Norilsk had said last year that its 1995 nickel output was 180,100 tonnes.
Prime-Tass said that 1996 copper output was 340,000 tonnes, up from what Norilsk had said was 1995 output of 338,700 tonnes.
Cobalt output was 3,151 tonnes. No comparative figures were available.
Prime-Tass said the metals group, one of the world's biggest producers of nickel, cobalt and platinum group metals, as well as of copper, planned to increase production of some metals by 2000.
Annual output of nickel would be raised to 213,000 tonnes by 2000, copper to 370,000 tonnes and cobalt to up to 4,000 tonnes.

Prime-Tass said the nickel processing part of the flagship combine in Norilsk would be closed down and that all nickel concentrates would be sent for processing to the Nadezhdinsky plant, but gave no further details.
Norilsk spokesman Sergei Vetchinin said a closure programme still had to be agreed with workers and management and that many questions still remained.
A Norilsk news release received after Prime-Tass ran its story said the company's targets were aimed at supporting production, reducing costs and improving quality.
Prime-Tass said the production targets were adopted by a RAO Norilsky Nickel 0#NKEL.RUO board meeting as part of a strategy to bring the metals group out of financial crisis.
The Norilsk release said Norilsk's mining strategy would involve halting work on disseminated and non-profitable ore mines and focusing on richer copper ores.

Ore mining in the Arctic Norilsk region would total 8.6 million tonnes by 2000, Tass said, not saying over what period of time. The Norilsk release said this would include 6.8 million tonnes of rich ores.
Mining would be carried out at the Oktyabrsky (October), Taimyrsky (Taimyr) and Skalisty deposits and the group would also begin exploiting the Gluboky mine, the company said.
The company's flagship plant is the Norilsk mining and enriching complex in Norilsk. Norilsk has ore reserves and mines across northwestern Russia.
Norilsk said the Pechenganickel unit would open new underground mines and produce about eight million tonnes of ore by 2000 over an unspecified time period.
Enriching processes at the flagship combine would be carried out at the Talnakhsky (Talnakhsk) factory, whose productivity would be improved with new technology.
Norilsk said artial modernisation of enriching facilities at the Pechenganickel combine would boost processing volumes to up to 600,000 tonnes a year.
Copper concentrate quality at the Norilsk combine would improve due to improvements in smelting technologies and reconstruction of anode processes at the Vanyukov furnaces.
The release said that all convertor matte from the Norilsk flagship combine and Pechenganickel would be processsed at Severonickel.

It said cobalt at the flagship combine and Severonickel would be produced under extraction technologies or be shifted to the Ufaleinickel and Yuzhuralnickel units where it would be produced on a tolling basis.
The release said Norilsk would set up a non-ferrous metals processing company called Norilsktsvetmetpererabotka and that it was considering collecting and processing secondary materials.
